newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tabcorp says has strong balance sheet.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tabcorp says has strong balance sheet.

text.p: Betting agency Tabcorp Holdings Ltd said on Monday it has a strong balance sheet to take advantage of expansion opportunities when they arise.

"With the privatisation process now completed, the company is well positioned to utilise its strong balance sheet to take advantage of opportunities for expansion as and when they arise," said Tabcorp managing director Ross Wilson.

Tabcorp earlier reported a net profit of A$87.17 million in the 1995/96 year. "The company is positioned in a growing market and will continue to focus on deriving maximum benefits from its existing wagering and gaming licences," Wilson said.

Wilson said Tabcorp expected there was still a growing demand for gaming and would continue to implement its rollout schedule for gaming machines in hotels and licenced clubs in 1996/97. He said the interim cap on gaming machines by the Victorian government in December 1995 was not expected to impact on the group's operations in the forthcoming year.
Wilson said the 1995/96 performance was a strong rise in revenue, while operating costs, excluding depreciation, were held at the same level a year earlier.
He said the company paid A$333.1 million to the Victorian state government in gaming taxes in 1995/96.
The result seemed to please investors, with Tabcorp shares hitting a record high at 10.55 a.m. (0055 GMT) of A$5.95, up 18 cents or 3.12 percent on Friday's close.
Tabcorp floated on the Australian Stock Exchange in August 1994 after it was privatised by the Victorian government.
